messages:
Maya G.: noticing increased 5xxs on internal L4 health checks between rack-7 and rack-9 over the last 10m. % of failed conns ~0.8% but spikes to 2% during bursts.
Jordan P.: ugh, same time frame as the ToR firmware push we did earlier? deploy-bot rolled v2.3-rt last night at 02:12 UTC.
deploy-bot: rollout completed for toR-image v2.3-rt on rack-6..rack-12 (02:12 UTC) :white_check_mark:
Maya G.: yes that aligns. symptoms: SYNs get retransmitted, connections sometimes switch path mid-handshake, then LB returns 502s.
Nate O. (oncall): did we see any ECMP hash changes? could be asymmetric hashing now. can someone pull flows for a heavy client ip -> internal service?
Rachel L.: grabbing flow logs from tofino-agg for rack-9. quick grep shows different hashes for packets in same 5-tuple during single session.
Jordan P.: that smells like a hash seed reset. On some ASICs a control-plane restart will re-seed hash and cause rebalancing; not normally causing drops though.
Maya G.: attaching snippets:
```
# from tofino-agg logs
SRC=10.2.71.84 DST=10.3.12.5 SPORT=52014 DPORT=443 HASH_BEFORE=0x1a2b HASH_AFTER=0x9f0c
PACKETS: SYN, SYN-ACK lost, retransmit
```
Nate O. (oncall): if packets flip path mid-TCP handshake we can end up at different ToR with closed state -> RST/timeout. That matches the 502s.
Jordan P.: quick mitigation: can we pin flows at the LB level with session-affinity for the next 30m? config change: set l4_session_timeout=300 and force per-conn sticky on source-ip+port hash.
Maya G.: trying now on the internal LB pool for cluster-ml-prod:```
> curl -X POST http://internal-lb/api/config -d '{"session_affinity":"src_port", "timeout":300}'
```
ops-bot: config update accepted for lb-cluster-ml-prod (03:02 UTC) :gear:
Maya G.: rolling monitor: healthcheck failures dropped to 0.2% after forcing affinity. good short-term sign.
Rachel L.: also seeing increased inter-rack latency variance (p50 stable, p99 jumps ~30ms) on same paths. reading RDMA counters for rack-9 NICs now.
Jordan P.: please check MTU too — if one ToR had a mismatch after the firmware push, large packets could fragment/drop. ping with DF set and mtu sweep?
Nate O. (oncall): running checks: ``ping -M do -s 8972 10.3.12.5`` shows fragmentation on path via tor-9 but ok via tor-7. MTU mismatch confirmed on tor-9 uplink (configured 9000 vs negotiated 8972).
Maya G.: ok that explains variance. but what about hash flips? two concurrent issues: MTU causing retransmits and firmware changed ECMP seed behavior.
Jordan P.: priority plan:
1) keep LB affinity for 1h to stabilize services.
2) roll back ToR firmware on rack-9 to previous build (v2.2-rt) if hardware supports quick rollback.
3) patch control-plane to persist hash seed across restarts.
4) audit MTU/LLDP configs across racks (scripted).
Rachel L.: created a quick check script: ``/opt/scripts/check-mtu-lldp.sh`` and ran across 20 racks — found 3 with mismatched MTU (rack-4, rack-9, rack-11).
Nate O. (oncall): initiating urgent change: tor-9 MTU corrected to 8972 and link flaps for 20s planned (03:12 UTC). will post when done.
ops-bot: change window scheduled: tor-9 mtu fix (03:12-03:15 UTC).
Maya G.: tor-9 MTU fix applied, monitoring. initial healthchecks back to normal, p99 latency normalized.
Jordan P.: long-term: add unit tests in firmware rollout job that verify hash seed persistence and LLDP/MTU sanity checks pre/post deploy.
Rachel L.: filing postmortem ticket and linking runbooks. pinging infra-ops to review LB affinity defaulting too long — could mask real issues.
Nate O. (oncall): thumbs up. will revert LB affinity after we confirm stability for 1h. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Maya G.: thanks — keeping oncall looped. will update thread if any regressions.
